teaches: a non-attaching letter with an attaching predecessor takes the incoming connection but never sends one out: final shape only
an attaching letter with both a capable predecessor and a following letter realizes the medial shape
the hamza-bearing alif variant is the same non-attaching member as bare alif, so word-start alone gives the standalone shape
the tied taa visually resembles the attaching letter ه but this lesson's closed inventory does not cover it; complete positional evidence still refuses a guess
the variant final a-spelling looks like the non-attaching alif but resemblance is not membership; it is refused, not classified by analogy
an unlisted hamza-bearing variant of a non-attaching letter is not silently folded into that letter's class; only the licensed alif variants are unified (con-r4)
an attaching letter's outgoing connection is never assumed; without declared evidence of a following letter the variant is refused, not defaulted to initial or final
no declared letter at all leaves nothing to classify

transfer: the same reasoning that a blocked predecessor yields no incoming connection (con-r2/con-r3) carries from the word-start case to a different non-attaching member preceded by another non-attaching letter
